note: Short hook. The first pick to learn single-pin picking with: lifts one pin at a time.
Medium hook. Reaches a pin set higher than its neighbours.
Deep hook. Reaches a high pin at the back past low pins in front of it.
Offset hook. The tip leans forward, so it reaches over a low pin onto the next one.
Swept hook, 1.2 mm tall. The shaft curves up in one smooth bend. Taller ones reach higher pins.
Swept hook, 1.6 mm tall. The shaft curves up in one smooth bend. Taller ones reach higher pins.
Swept hook, 2 mm tall. The shaft curves up in one smooth bend. Taller ones reach higher pins.
Swept hook, 2.5 mm tall. The shaft curves up in one smooth bend. Taller ones reach higher pins.
Swept hook, 3 mm tall. The shaft curves up in one smooth bend. Taller ones reach higher pins.
Swept hook, 3.5 mm tall. The shaft curves up in one smooth bend. Taller ones reach higher pins.
Swept hook, 4 mm tall. The shaft curves up in one smooth bend. Taller ones reach higher pins.
Swept hook, 5 mm tall. The shaft curves up in one smooth bend. Taller ones reach higher pins.
Small half-diamond. Single pins in tight keyways, and gentle raking.
Medium half-diamond. The all-round shape: single pins, raking, wafer locks.
Large half-diamond. Easier to feel on wide keyways and wafer locks.
Steep half-diamond. Steeper sides reach a higher pin than the medium one.
Bogota, two humps. Rock it up and down while pulling out slowly.
Bogota, three humps. As the two-hump one, covers more pins at once.
Snake rake. Waves up and down; scrub it in and out with light tension.
City rake (L-rake). Shaped like a key's cuts; rock it to set several pins at once.
Triple-peak rake. Three sharp peaks; rock it while easing it out.
Half-ball. For wafer locks (desks, cabinets, cars); also lifts single pins.
Ball. Rides over wafers without catching; rock it in and out.
Double ball (snowman). Rocks two wafers at a time.
Zig-zag rake for wafer locks.
Wide rocker. Two tall humps for rocking wafer locks.

Comb for Kwikset, 5 pins. Slide it in along the bottom of the keyway until the stop touches the lock face, then lift: the 5 mm teeth push every pin stack above the shear line. Not for locks with anti-comb pins.

Comb for Schlage, 5 pins. Slide it in along the bottom of the keyway until the stop touches the lock face, then lift: the 5 mm teeth push every pin stack above the shear line. Not for locks with anti-comb pins.

Comb for Schlage, 6 pins. Slide it in along the bottom of the keyway until the stop touches the lock face, then lift: the 5 mm teeth push every pin stack above the shear line. Not for locks with anti-comb pins.
Warded pick, L shape, 4.0 mm bit. For cheap warded padlocks: the bit reaches round the wards to the catch.
Warded pick, L shape, 5.5 mm bit.
Warded pick, L shape, 6.8 mm bit.
Warded pick, T shape, 2.5 mm bit each side.
Warded pick, T shape, 3.5 mm bit each side.
Lever lifter, 3.5 mm. For UK lever mortice locks: lifts one lever at a time. Use with a curtain wrench.
Lever lifter, 5.0 mm. For levers that sit higher.
Curtain wrench, 6 mm bit. The tension tool for lever locks: it turns the bolt stump. Check the bit fits your keyhole.
Curtain wrench, 8 mm bit.
Dimple pick blank. Bend the end 90° at the two notches to make a 2.0 × 2.5 mm flag.
